metadata.title: Compressed Sensing
metadata.venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, vol. 52, no. 4, pp. 1289-1306
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: $\ell_p$ ball / sparsity class
nodes.statement: The class $\Theta_{p,N}(C) = \{ \theta \in \mathbb{R}^N : \sum_i |\theta_i|^p \leq C^p \}$ for $0 < p \leq 1$ encodes sparsity/compressibility of transform coefficients.
nodes.statement_clean: Object class defined by an $\ell_p$ constraint on transform coefficients with $0 < p \le 1$, encoding compressibility.

nodes.name: Best $m$-term approximation
nodes.statement: Letting $\theta_{[m]}$ denote the vector $\theta$ with all but the $m$ largest coefficients set to zero, $\|\theta - \theta_{[m]}\|_2 \leq C \cdot m^{-r}$ with $r = 1/p - 1/2$ when $\theta \in \Theta_{p,N}(C)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Truncating to the $m$ largest coefficients gives error decaying like $m^{-(1/p-1/2)}$ for vectors in the $\ell_p$ ball.

nodes.name: Information operator and minimax error
nodes.statement: An information operator $\mathcal{I}_n(x) = (\xi_1(x),\dots,\xi_n(x))$ uses nonadaptive sampling kernels $\xi_i$. The minimax error is $E_n(\mathcal{X}) = \inf_{\mathcal{I}_n,\mathcal{A}} \sup_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \|x - \mathcal{A}(\mathcal{I}_n(x))\|_2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Worst-case error over a class for the best pair of nonadaptive linear measurements and reconstruction algorithm.

nodes.name: Gel'fand $n$-width
nodes.statement: Definition 1.1: $d^n(\mathcal{X}, \|\cdot\|_2) = \inf_{V_n} \sup\{ \|x\|_2 : x \in \mathcal{X} \cap V_n^{\perp} \}$ where the infimum is over $n$-dimensional linear subspaces $V_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gel'fand $n$-width: smallest possible radius of the section of $\mathcal{X}$ cut by an $n$-codimensional subspace.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov $n$-width
nodes.statement: Definition 1.2: $d_n(\mathcal{X}, \|\cdot\|_2) = \inf_{V_n} \sup_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \inf_{y \in V_n} \|x - y\|_2$ where the infimum is over $n$-dimensional linear subspaces $V_n$ of $\mathbb{R}^N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Kolmogorov $n$-width: best worst-case approximation of $\mathcal{X}$ by an $n$-dimensional subspace.

nodes.name: CS matrix conditions CS1, CS2, CS3
nodes.statement: An $n \times m$ matrix $\Phi$ is a CS matrix with parameters $(\eta, \rho)$ if (CS1) the minimal singular value of any $\Phi_J$ with $|J| < \rho \, n / \log(m)$ exceeds $\eta_1 > 0$; (CS2) every such range $V_J$ affords a near-spherical section of the $\ell_1$ ball; (CS3) the quotient norm $\|\cdot\|_{Q,J}$ on $V_J$ is comparable to the $\ell_1$ norm.
nodes.statement_clean: Three structural conditions on a measurement matrix: (CS1) minimal singular values, (CS2) near-spherical sections, (CS3) quotient-norm control.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-isometry between $\ell_2$ and $\ell_1$
nodes.statement: Definition 7.1: $V$ offers an $\epsilon$-isometry between $\ell_2^{|J|}$ and $\ell_1^n$ if $(1-\epsilon)\sqrt{n} \, \|y\|_2 \leq \|y\|_1 \leq (1+\epsilon)\sqrt{n} \, \|y\|_2$ for all $y \in V$.
nodes.statement_clean: A subspace gives an almost-spherical section of the $\ell_1$ ball when its $\ell_1$ and (rescaled) $\ell_2$ norms agree up to factor $1 \pm \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Maximal concentration $\nu_*$
nodes.statement: For $J \subset \{1,\dots,m\}$ and $\alpha \in \ker(\Phi)$, the concentration $\nu(\alpha,J) = \|\alpha_J\|_1 / \|\alpha\|_1$. The maximal concentration $\nu_*(\rho;\Phi)$ is the supremum over $|J| \leq \rho \, n / \log m$ and $\alpha \in \ker(\Phi) \setminus \{0\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Maximal fraction of $\ell_1$ mass any small index set $J$ can carry for a vector in the nullspace of $\Phi$.

nodes.name: Weak-$\ell_p$ ball
nodes.statement: $x$ lies in the weak-$\ell_p$ ball of radius $C$ if its decreasing rearrangement satisfies $|x|_{(k)} \leq C \cdot k^{-1/p}$ for all $k$. The smallest such $C$ is the weak-$\ell_p$ quasinorm $\|x\|_{w\ell_p}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Vectors whose sorted entries decay at least like $k^{-1/p}$.

nodes.name: Tight frame
nodes.statement: A tight frame is a collection $\{\psi_i\}$ which, when joined as columns of an $N \times d$ matrix $\Psi$ with $d \geq N$, satisfies $\Psi \Psi^T = I$ (Parseval relation) and $x = \Psi \theta$ with $\theta = \Psi^T x$.
nodes.statement_clean: Overcomplete dictionary satisfying a Parseval reconstruction identity.

nodes.name: Compressed sensing reconstruction
nodes.statement: Given $y = \mathcal{I}_n(x) \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \ll N$, recover an unknown signal $x \in \mathbb{R}^N$ assumed to have transform coefficients $\theta = \Psi^T x$ in $\Theta_{p,N}(C)$, with error close to the best $m$-term approximation.
nodes.statement_clean: Reconstruct a high-dimensional compressible signal from far fewer nonadaptive linear measurements than its ambient dimension.

nodes.name: $(P_1)$ Basis Pursuit / $\ell_1$-minimization
nodes.statement: $(P_1)$: $\min \|\theta\|_1$ subject to $y_k = \langle \psi_k, x \rangle$, $k = 1,\dots,n$, with $x = \Psi \theta$. Find the minimum-$\ell_1$ coefficient vector consistent with the measurements.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex $\ell_1$ minimization over coefficient vectors compatible with the data.

nodes.name: $(P_p)$ feasible $\ell_p$-minimization
nodes.statement: $(P_p)$: $\min \|\theta\|_p$ subject to $y = \mathcal{I}_n(x)$, for $0 < p \leq 1$. Generalizes Basis Pursuit; nonconvex when $p < 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Find the minimum-$\ell_p$-quasinorm coefficient vector matching the measurements.

nodes.name: $(P_0)$ sparsest-solution problem
nodes.statement: $(P_0)$: $\min \|\theta\|_0$ subject to $y = \mathcal{I}_n(\Psi \theta)$, where $\|\theta\|_0 = \#\{i : \theta_i \neq 0\}$. Combinatorial: search for the sparsest exact representation.
nodes.statement_clean: Combinatorial problem of finding the sparsest coefficient vector explaining the data.

nodes.name: Sparsity bound (I.1)
nodes.statement: $\sum_i |\theta_i|^p \leq R^p$ for some $0 < p \leq 1$ and some $R > 0$.

nodes.name: Truncation error (I.2)
nodes.statement: $\|\theta - \theta_{[m]}\|_2 \leq C_p \cdot m^{-r}$, $r = 1/p - 1/2$, for $\theta$ obeying (I.1).

nodes.name: Compressed-sensing rate (I.3)
nodes.statement: $E_n(\mathcal{X}_{p,N}) \leq C_p \cdot (n / \log(N))^{-r}$ for $n,N \to \infty$ with $n / \log(N) \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Width-error equivalence (I.4)-(I.5)
nodes.statement: (I.4) $E_n(\mathcal{X}_{p,N}) \asymp d^n(\mathcal{X}_{p,N})$ for $p = 1$; (I.5) for $0 < p < 1$, $d^n \leq E_n \leq 2^{1/p} d^n$.

nodes.name: Gel'fand-Kolmogorov duality (I.6)
nodes.statement: $d^n(B_{p'}^N, \ell_q^N) = d_n(B_q^N, \ell_{p'}^N)$ where $1/p + 1/p' = 1$, valid for $1 \leq p \leq \infty$.

nodes.name: Linear program form of $(P_1)$ (IV.1)
nodes.statement: $(LP)$: $\min \sum_i (u_i + v_i)$ subject to $A(u - v) = y$, $u, v \geq 0$, where $A = \Phi \Psi^T$ and $\theta = u - v$.

nodes.name: Holographic kernel (VI.1)
nodes.statement: $\xi_k(x) = \sum_{\mu} \Phi_{k,\mu} \langle \psi_\mu, x \rangle$, where the sum runs over an enumeration of the wavelets $\psi_\mu$.

nodes.name: Weak-$\ell_p$ truncation (V.1)
nodes.statement: $\|x - x_{[m]}\|_2 \leq C_p \cdot \|x\|_{w\ell_p} \cdot m^{-r}$ for $r = 1/p - 1/2$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1: compressed-sensing rate
nodes.statement: For $0 < p < 1$ (and $p = 1$) and problem sizes $(n,m,N)$ with $n,m \to \infty$, $n / \log(N) \to \infty$, there exists $C = C(p,\rho)$ so that $E_n(\mathcal{X}_{p,N}) \leq C \cdot (n / \log(N))^{-r}$, $r = 1/p - 1/2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimax reconstruction error over $\Theta_{p,N}(C)$ from $n$ nonadaptive measurements decays as $(n/\log N)^{-(1/p - 1/2)}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 2: adaptive information is no help
nodes.statement: For $0 < p \leq 1$, there is $C^*$ so that $E_n^*(\mathcal{X}_{p,N}) \geq C^* \cdot E_{2n}(\mathcal{X}_{p,N})$, where $E_n^*$ is the minimax error under adaptive information.
nodes.statement_clean: Allowing adaptive measurements changes the minimax error only by a constant factor.

nodes.name: Theorem 3: width-error equivalence
nodes.statement: For $0 < p \leq 1$ and $\mathcal{X} = \mathcal{X}_{p,N}$: (I.4) when $p \geq 1$, $d^n \leq E_n \leq 2 \, d^n$; (I.5) for $0 < p < 1$, $d^n \leq E_n \leq 2^{1/p} d^n$.
nodes.statement_clean: Minimax error and Gel'fand $n$-width are equivalent up to constants for these classes.

nodes.name: Kashin-Garnaev-Gluskin (KGG)
nodes.statement: Theorem 4 (Kashin, Garnaev, Gluskin): For all $n$ and $N$, $d_n(B_1^N, \ell_2^N) \asymp \min\{1, \sqrt{\log(N/n)/n}\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharp asymptotics for the Kolmogorov $n$-widths of the $\ell_1$ ball in $\ell_2$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5: near-optimal CS info + Basis Pursuit
nodes.statement: For $(n,m,N)$ obeying $m \sim N$, $n/m \to 0$, $n/\log(m) \to \infty$, and $\mathcal{I}_n$ derived from a CS matrix with parameters $(\eta,\rho)$, the operator $\mathcal{I}_n$ is near-optimal and the algorithm $\mathcal{A}_{1,n}$ solving $(P_1)$ is also near-optimal: $E_n(\mathcal{I}_n,\mathcal{A}_{1,n};\mathcal{X}_{p,N}) \leq C \cdot (n/\log(m))^{-r}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Random CS measurements combined with $\ell_1$ minimization achieve the near-optimal rate of Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Theorem 6: ubiquity of CS matrices
nodes.statement: There exist $\eta = \eta(\rho)$ and $\rho_0 > 0$ depending only on the regime so that the proportion of $n \times m$ matrices (with i.i.d. uniform columns on the sphere) satisfying CS1-CS3 with parameters $(\eta,\rho)$ eventually exceeds $1 - e^{-\beta n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A random matrix from the uniform measure on column-normalized $n \times m$ matrices satisfies the CS conditions with overwhelming probability.
conclusions: Probability that $\Phi$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with $(\eta,\rho)$ tends to $1$ exponentially fast

nodes.name: Theorem 7: CS matrices yield near-optimal widths
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ is a sequence of CS matrices with $\eta,\rho$ positive and independent of $n$, then for each $0 < p \leq 1$ there is $C = C(p,\eta,\rho)$ so that $w(\ker\Phi, \mathcal{X}_{p,N}) \leq C \cdot (n/\log(m))^{-r}$, $r = 1/p - 1/2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Nullspaces of CS matrices give Gel'fand widths matching the optimal rate.

nodes.name: Theorem 8: $\ell_0$-$\ell_1$ equivalence for sparse solutions
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with positive $\eta,\rho$, there exists $\rho^* = \rho^*(\eta,\rho)$ so that whenever $(P_0)$ has a solution with at most $\rho^* \, n / \log(m)$ nonzeros, then $(P_0)$ and $(P_1)$ have the same unique solution.
nodes.statement_clean: When the data admit a sufficiently sparse representation, $\ell_1$ minimization recovers it exactly.
assumptions: $(P_0)$ has a solution with $\leq \rho^* \, n / \log m$ nonzeros
conclusions: $(P_0)$ and $(P_1)$ have the same unique solution

nodes.name: Theorem 9: Basis Pursuit near-optimal for $0 < p \leq 1$
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with positive $\eta,\rho$, there is $C = C(p,\eta,\rho)$ so that the solution $\hat\theta_{1,n}$ of $(P_1)$ obeys $\|\hat\theta_{1,n} - \theta\|_2 \leq C \cdot (n/\log m)^{-r}$ for all $\theta \in \Theta_{p,N}(C)$, $0 < p \leq 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: $\ell_1$ reconstruction extends the near-optimal guarantee to the full range $0 < p \leq 1$, including the nonconvex sparsity regime.

nodes.name: Theorem 10: random matrices satisfy CS1-CS3
nodes.statement: Let $\Phi$ be an $n \times m$ matrix with columns drawn i.i.d. uniformly from $S^{n-1}$. For some $\eta,\rho > 0$, conditions CS1-CS3 hold for $\Phi$ with overwhelming probability for all large $n$ (under $m \sim N$, $n/m \to 0$, $n/\log(m) \to \infty$).
nodes.statement_clean: Reformulation of Theorem 6: random spherical-column matrices are CS matrices with high probability.

nodes.name: Theorem 11: alternative CS conditions A1, A2
nodes.statement: Suppose $\Phi$ obeys A1 (maximal concentration $\nu_*(\rho) \leq C_1$) and A2 (width $w(\ker\Phi, B_1^m) \leq C_2 \cdot (n/\log m)^{-1/2}$). Then for $0 < p \leq 1$ and some $C$, the solution of $(P_1)$ obeys $\|\hat\theta - \theta\|_2 \leq C \cdot (n/\log m)^{-r}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Two alternative concentration/width conditions on $\Phi$ also imply near-optimal Basis Pursuit recovery.

nodes.name: Lemma 3.1: feasible-point near-optimality
nodes.statement: Let $\hat x_{F,n} \in \mathcal{X}_y$ where $y = \mathcal{I}_n(x)$ and $\mathcal{I}_n$ is an optimal information operator. Then for $x \in \mathcal{X}$, $\|x - \hat x_{F,n}\|_2 \leq 2 \cdot E_n(\mathcal{X})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any feasible point is within a factor 2 of the central-algorithm minimax error.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.1: nonconcentration in nullspace
nodes.statement: If $\Phi$ satisfies CS1-CS3 with constants $\eta,\rho$, there is $\mu = \mu(\eta,\rho)$ so that for $|J| \leq \rho \, n / \log m$ and any $\alpha \in \ker\Phi$, $\|\alpha_J\|_1 \leq \mu \cdot \|\alpha\|_1$.
nodes.statement_clean: No small index set can carry more than a $\mu$-fraction of $\ell_1$ mass for nullspace vectors.

nodes.name: Lemma 4.2: $\ell_0$ stability lemma
nodes.statement: Let $x \in \mathbb{R}^N$, $x_{[m]}$ its $m$-truncation. If $\|x - x_{[m]}\|_1 \leq \epsilon$ and $y = \mathcal{I}_n(x)$, then the solution $\hat x$ of $(P_1)$ obeys $\|\hat x - x\|_1 \leq C \cdot \epsilon$ with $C$ depending on $\eta,\rho$.
nodes.statement_clean: $\ell_1$ minimization is stable under small $\ell_1$ perturbations of the signal.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.1: minimal eigenvalue control (CS1)
nodes.statement: Consider sequences with $n/\log(m) \to \infty$. Define the event $\Omega_n^1$ that $\sigma_{\min}(\Phi_J) \geq \eta_1$ for every $|J| \leq \rho \, n / \log m$. For each $\eta_1 > 0$, there is $\rho > 0$ small enough that $\Pr[\Omega_n^1] \to 1$ exponentially.
nodes.statement_clean: Random CS matrices have uniformly bounded minimal singular values over all small column subsets, with overwhelming probability.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.2: large deviations on min eigenvalue (single $J$)
nodes.statement: For $|J| < \rho \, n / \log m$ and the event $\Omega_J^1$ that $\sigma_{\min}(\Phi_J) > \eta_1$, there is $\beta > 0$ so that $\Pr[(\Omega_J^1)^c] \leq e^{-\beta n}$ uniformly in $J$.
nodes.statement_clean: For each fixed small subset $J$, the minimum singular value of $\Phi_J$ is bounded below with exponentially-good probability.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.3: combining principle (Boole-style)
nodes.statement: If events $\Omega_J$ obey $\Pr[\Omega_J^c] \leq e^{-\beta n}$ for each $J$ with $|J| \leq k$, and $k \leq \rho \, n / \log m$, then $\Pr[\bigcap_J \Omega_J] \to 1$ for sufficiently small $\rho$.
nodes.statement_clean: Exponentially-good per-subset bounds combine via union bound to a uniform bound over all small subsets.
assumptions: $\Pr[\Omega_J^c] \leq e^{-\beta n}$ for each $J$ with $|J| \leq k$

nodes.name: Lemma 7.4: spherical sections (CS2)
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega_n^2$ be the event that every $V_J$ with $|J| \leq \rho \, n / \log m$ offers an $\epsilon$-isometry between $\ell_2^{|J|}$ and $\ell_1^n$. For each $\epsilon > 0$, there is $\rho > 0$ so that $\Pr[\Omega_n^2] \to 1$ exponentially.
nodes.statement_clean: Almost-spherical sections of the $\ell_1$ ball are uniformly available across all small subspaces with high probability.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.5: individual spherical section
nodes.statement: Fix $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ and choose $\rho$ so that two technical inequalities (VII.2)-(VII.3) hold. For a single $J$ with $|J| < \rho \, n / \log m$, the probability that $V_J$ furnishes an $\epsilon$-isometry tends to one with the gap controlled by $\delta$.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-subset spherical-sections bound underlying Lemma 7.4.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.6: uniform sign-pattern embedding
nodes.statement: Fix $\rho > 0$ small. For $\sigma > 0$, set $\gamma$ as in (VII.4). On an event $\Omega_n^3$ with $\Pr[\Omega_n^3] \to 1$, for each $J$ with $|J| < \rho \, n / \log m$ and each sign pattern $z \in \{\pm 1\}^J$, there is $w \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with $\|w\|_\infty \leq \gamma$ and $\|\Phi^T w - z\|_{w\ell_p} \leq \sigma$.
nodes.statement_clean: Every sign pattern on a small index set is uniformly approximately embedded in the dual ball of $\Phi$.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.7: individual sign-pattern embedding
nodes.statement: For a fixed $J$ with $|J| < \rho \, n / \log m$, an iterative algorithm produces $w$ with $\|w\|_\infty \leq \gamma$ and $\Phi_J^T w = z$ on the event $\Omega_J^3$, with $\Pr[(\Omega_J^3)^c]$ controlled exponentially.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-subset version of Lemma 7.6, proven by an iterative dual-feasibility algorithm.
conclusions: Iterative algorithm outputs $w$ with the embedding bound (VII.9)-(VII.11)

nodes.name: Lemma 7.8: standard large-deviations bounds
nodes.statement: Let $Z_i$ be i.i.d. $N(0,1)$. Then $\Pr[\sum Z_i^2 > n(1+t)] \leq e^{-c n t^2}$ and $\Pr[\sum Z_i^2 < n(1-t)] \leq e^{-c n t^2}$ for $t \in (0,1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard chi-squared concentration inequalities used to bound trajectory descriptors.
conclusions: $\Pr[|\sum Z_i^2 - n| > nt] \leq 2 e^{-c n t^2}$

nodes.name: Corollary 4.1: Basis Pursuit inherits near-optimality
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{I}_n$ achieves $E_n(\mathcal{I}_n;\mathcal{X}) \leq C \cdot (n/\log m)^{-r}$ for some $C$, then the Basis Pursuit algorithm $\mathcal{A}_{1,n}$ achieves $\|x - \hat x_{1,n}\|_2 \leq 2 C \cdot (n/\log m)^{-r}$ for all $x \in \mathcal{X}_{p,N}$ with $p = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Whenever the information operator is near-optimal in the $p = 1$ case, Basis Pursuit reconstruction is near-optimal too.

nodes.name: Garnaev-Gluskin Kolmogorov-width estimate (cited)
nodes.statement: Garnaev and Gluskin [9], building on Kashin [10]: $d_n(B_1^N, \ell_2^N) \asymp \sqrt{(\log(N/n) + 1) / n}$ for $1 \leq n \leq N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Sharp Kolmogorov-width asymptotics of the $\ell_1$ ball; the foundational external result powering Theorem 1 in the $p = 1$ case.

nodes.name: Carl's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: Carl [18]: There is a constant $c_p$ so that the Gel'fand $n$-widths dominate the entropy numbers: $e_n(\mathcal{X}) \leq c_p \cdot d^n(\mathcal{X})$ for compact $\mathcal{X}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited entropy/width inequality used in the lower-bound part of the proof of Theorem 1.

nodes.name: $p$-triangle inequality (cited)
nodes.statement: For $0 < p \leq 1$ and $a, b \geq 0$: $(a + b)^p \leq a^p + b^p$. Also $\|x + y\|_p^p \leq \|x\|_p^p + \|y\|_p^p$ on $\ell_p$ quasinormed spaces.
nodes.statement_clean: $p$-triangle inequality used throughout the $p < 1$ arguments.

nodes.name: Almost-spherical sections / Dvoretsky-Milman (cited)
nodes.statement: Slicing the unit ball of a Banach space by an appropriate finite-dimensional subspace yields a section that is essentially spherical.
nodes.statement_clean: Cited Banach-space-geometry result motivating CS2.

nodes.name: Central algorithm (OR/IBC)
nodes.statement: Given information $y = \mathcal{I}_n(x)$, return the Chebyshev center of the feasibility set $\mathcal{X}_y = \{x' \in \mathcal{X} : \mathcal{I}_n(x') = y\}$.

nodes.name: Feasible-point method
nodes.statement: Given $y = \mathcal{I}_n(x)$, return any element $\hat x_{F,n} \in \mathcal{X}_y$. Lemma 3.1 shows it is within factor 2 of the central algorithm.

nodes.name: Basis Pursuit / $\ell_1$-minimization
nodes.statement: Iterative-LP procedure that solves $(P_1)$: $\min \|\theta\|_1$ s.t. $y = \Phi \Psi^T \theta$, then returns $\hat x_{1,n} = \Psi \hat\theta$. Cast as the LP (IV.1) and solved by interior-point methods.
nodes.pseudocode: 1. Form $A = \Phi \Psi^T$. 2. Solve LP: $\min \sum_i (u_i + v_i)$ s.t. $A(u-v) = y$, $u,v \geq 0$. 3. Set $\hat\theta = u - v$, return $\hat x = \Psi \hat\theta$.

nodes.name: Iterative dual-feasibility / sign-pattern embedding algorithm
nodes.statement: Iterative procedure (from [11]) that, starting from a near-feasible point $w_0$ for the dual program, produces a strictly dual-feasible $w$ approximating any prescribed sign pattern $z$ on $J$.

nodes.name: Bump Algebra model for spectra
nodes.statement: A spectrum is modeled as $f(t) = \sum_j \alpha_j g((t - t_j)/s_j)$ with energy constraint $\sum_j |\alpha_j| \leq C$. Wavelet coefficients at scale $j$ obey $\|\theta_j\|_1 \leq C$. CS allows $O(N^{1/3} \log N)$ measurements vs $N$.
nodes.statement_clean: Spectral lines model where compressed sensing reduces $N$ pixel samples to roughly the cube root.

nodes.name: Bounded Variation model for images
nodes.statement: Images $f \in BV([0,1]^2)$ with $\mathrm{TV}(f) \leq C$ have wavelet coefficients $\|\theta_j\|_1 \leq C$. CS allows $O(N^{1/2} \log N)$ measurements vs $N$ pixels for comparable accuracy.
nodes.statement_clean: BV image model where compressed sensing reduces sampling to roughly the square root of the linear rate.

nodes.name: Piecewise $C^2$ images with $C^2$ edges (curvelets)
nodes.statement: Cartoon images with $C^2$ smooth pieces separated by $C^2$ curves of total length $\leq L$. Curvelet coefficients obey weak-$\ell_p$ with $p = 2/3$. CS allows $O(N^{1/4})$ measurements (the fourth root).
nodes.statement_clean: Cartoon images with $C^2$ edges; curvelet sparsity yields a fourth-root sampling rate via CS.

nodes.name: Holographic measurement kernels
nodes.statement: The CS sampling kernels $\xi_k$ are not pixel samples but holographic functionals: each $\xi_k$ depends on every transform coefficient (compare equation VI.1). Reconstruction must be nonlinear.

nodes.name: Universality of the CS scheme
nodes.statement: The same $\Phi$ works for any $(p, R)$: a single near-optimal information operator combined with Basis Pursuit reconstructs any compressible signal class without knowing $p$ or $R$ in advance.

nodes.name: Partial Fourier ensemble (Candes-Romberg-Tao, Gilbert et al.)
nodes.statement: Candes-Romberg-Tao [13] show that random partial Fourier matrices satisfy condition A1; Gilbert et al. [12] suggest A2 holds in a related ensemble. Candes-Tao [47] indicate A2 holds for the uniformly sampled partial Fourier ensemble modulo polylogs.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7
nodes.statement: Bound the width $w(\ker\Phi, \mathcal{X}_{p,N})$ via the optimization $\max \|\theta\|_2$ s.t. $\Phi \Psi^T \theta = 0$, $\|\theta\|_p \leq C$. Split $\theta = \theta_{[m]} + \theta_J^c$ and apply CS1, CS2, CS3 in succession to bound each piece.

nodes.name: Set up split into $\theta_{[m]}$ and tail
nodes.statement: Choose $m$ so $m / \log(m) \sim n$. Let $J$ index the $m$ largest entries of $\theta$; partition $\theta = \theta_J + \theta_{J^c}$. Apply (I.2) to bound $\|\theta_{J^c}\|_2$.

nodes.name: Apply CS3 to control quotient norm of $\theta_J$
nodes.statement: Use $\Phi \theta = 0$ to write $\Phi_J \theta_J = -\Phi_{J^c} \theta_{J^c}$. Then CS3 gives $\|\theta_J\|_{Q,J} \leq C \, \|\theta_{J^c}\|_1 / \sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Apply CS2 to relate $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ on $V_J$
nodes.statement: On $V_J$, the spherical-section property (CS2) gives $\|\theta_J\|_2 \leq C \, \|\theta_J\|_1 / \sqrt{|J|}$.

nodes.name: Apply CS1 and conclude
nodes.statement: CS1 transfers the bound from $\Phi_J \theta_J$ back to $\|\theta_J\|_2$. Combining with the tail bound from Step 1 gives $w(\ker\Phi,\mathcal{X}_{p,N}) \leq C (n/\log m)^{-r}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8
nodes.statement: Show that if $\theta$ has $\leq \rho^* n / \log m$ nonzeros, then it is the unique minimizer of $(P_1)$. Use Lemma 4.1: any nullspace direction can carry at most fraction $\mu$ of $\ell_1$ mass on a small set, contradicting any cheaper feasible vector.

nodes.name: Setup: assume sparser solution exists
nodes.statement: Suppose $\theta$ supported on $J$ with $|J| < \rho^* n / \log m$ solves $(P_0)$, and let $\theta'$ be any other $(P_1)$-feasible vector.

nodes.name: Difference is in nullspace
nodes.statement: $\alpha = \theta' - \theta \in \ker\Phi$, so the concentration bound applies: $\|\alpha_J\|_1 \leq \mu \|\alpha\|_1$.

nodes.name: Compare $\ell_1$ norms
nodes.statement: $\|\theta'\|_1 \geq \|\theta\|_1 + (1 - 2\mu) \|\alpha_{J^c}\|_1 > \|\theta\|_1$ when $\mu < 1/2$, contradicting $\theta'$ being a minimizer.

nodes.name: Conclude uniqueness
nodes.statement: Hence $\theta = \theta'$, i.e., $(P_0)$ and $(P_1)$ share the same unique solution.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9
nodes.statement: Use the framework of Theorem 7. Let $\hat\theta$ solve $(P_1)$ and write $\theta = \theta_{[m]} + (\theta - \theta_{[m]})$. Apply Lemma 4.1 to bound the $J^c$-mass of $\hat\theta - \theta$, then Lemma 4.2 ($\ell_0$ stability) and homogeneity to conclude.

nodes.name: Choose $m$ and indexing set $J$
nodes.statement: Set $m = m(n)$ with $m / \log m \sim n$. Let $J$ index the $m$ largest entries of $\theta$ in $|\cdot|$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4.1 (concentration bound)
nodes.statement: Since $\hat\theta - \theta \in \ker\Phi$, Lemma 4.1 gives $\|(\hat\theta - \theta)_J\|_1 \leq \mu \|(\hat\theta - \theta)\|_1$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 4.2 ($\ell_1$-stability)
nodes.statement: Lemma 4.2 yields $\|\hat\theta - \theta\|_1 \leq C \|\theta - \theta_{[m]}\|_1$, which by (I.2) is $\leq C' m^{-r+1/2}$.

nodes.name: Conclude by homogeneity
nodes.statement: Combine with the $\ell_2$ bound on $V_J$ from CS2 and homogeneity to get $\|\hat\theta - \theta\|_2 \leq C (n / \log m)^{-r}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10 (sketch)
nodes.statement: Prove that random spherical-column matrices satisfy CS1, CS2, CS3 separately: CS1 via Lemma 7.1 (eigenvalue control), CS2 via Lemma 7.4 (spherical sections), CS3 via Lemma 7.6 (sign-pattern embedding). Combine by union bound.

nodes.name: CS1 via Lemma 7.1
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 7.1: $\Pr[$CS1 with $(\eta_1,\rho_1)] \to 1$ exponentially.

nodes.name: CS2 via Lemma 7.4
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 7.4: $\Pr[$CS2 with $(\eta_2,\rho_2)] \to 1$ exponentially.

nodes.name: CS3 via Lemma 7.6
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 7.6: $\Pr[$CS3 with $(\eta_3,\rho_3)] \to 1$ exponentially.

nodes.name: Combine via Boole's inequality
nodes.statement: Take $\eta = \min(\eta_i)$, $\rho = \min(\rho_i)$. Then $\Pr[$CS1-CS3 hold simultaneously$] \geq 1 - \sum_i \Pr[\Omega_n^{i,c}] \to 1$.
